title: Variation in Tactics
coreMove: Hold rules loosely enough to disobey a bad route, bad order, or bad temptation when the situation changes.
sourcePressure: The source lists roads not to follow, armies not to attack, towns not to besiege, positions not to contest, commands not to obey, then ties tactical variation to blended advantage and disadvantage and five dangerous faults.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Using flexibility as an excuse for improvising without discipline.

sourceAnchors.name: commands of the sovereign which must not be obeyed
sourceAnchors.detail: The source explicitly says some commands should not be obeyed when tactical reality makes them destructive.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Good judgment includes knowing when obedience would betray the purpose of the order.

sourceAnchors.name: the five dangerous faults
sourceAnchors.detail: Recklessness, cowardice, hasty temper, sensitivity to shame, and over-solicitude can each ruin command.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A tactic often fails because a private fault grabs the steering wheel.

hook: A battlefield metaphor imported into a modern office before the actual choice is visible
A generic sentence about strategy being planning under pressure
counterintuition: The obvious move is not always best; the opposite move is smarter
Winning is not about strength but about strategy
tryThisNow: Set a timer and think about your next battle
Write down your goal and one obstacle

exampleSpecs.domain: newsroom deciding whether to publish during an unfolding hostage situation
exampleSpecs.audience: managing editor with a confirmed detail and police request
exampleSpecs.stakes: publishing first could endanger the people inside
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 11:03 p.m., Laura overrides the newsroom rule to publish confirmed facts when the fact itself would reveal police position.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a police scanner beside an unpublished headline

exampleSpecs.domain: mountain rescue team ordered onto an unsafe ridge
exampleSpecs.audience: team leader receiving pressure from command
exampleSpecs.stakes: following the route could create more casualties
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Ice rattles against Ben's visor as he refuses the shortest ridge and chooses the longer treeline route that keeps rescuers alive.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: ice rattling against a helmet visor

exampleSpecs.domain: investment committee rejecting an attractive distressed asset
exampleSpecs.audience: portfolio manager during a market selloff
exampleSpecs.stakes: a cheap price hides liquidity terms that could trap the fund
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: What if the discount is the bait and the lockup is the battlefield?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a term sheet with a red lockup clause

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital surgeon deciding whether to continue a planned procedure
exampleSpecs.audience: lead surgeon after unexpected anatomy appears
exampleSpecs.stakes: pushing through preserves schedule but raises patient risk
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The plan was correct until the anatomy changed, Hanna says, then pauses the procedure for imaging instead of protecting her pride.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a frozen laparoscopic image on a monitor

exampleSpecs.domain: railway dispatcher rerouting trains during signal failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: keeping the timetable could send trains into a blind section
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The signal board goes dark in one block while Tomas cancels the proud express slot to preserve the network.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a dark block on a signal board

exampleSpecs.domain: consumer-products team refusing a viral packaging trend
exampleSpecs.stakes: a flashy package could break shelf stability and damage returns
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Adaeze one toppled test display to treat shame about looking slow as a dangerous fault, not a reason to copy the trend.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a toppled shelf display in a test aisle
